subject: Spending Moratorium and Financial Reporting Debate
overview: The Council debated the city's financial health, tabling a proposed spending moratorium in favor of mandating quarterly reports and monthly warrant articles from the Finance Director. The body also discussed administrative communication failures following a high-profile assault at Medford High School and resident complaints regarding new parking meter installations.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location
items.summary: Approved the relocation of gas lines on Walnut and Metcalfe Streets to accommodate city water main work, with the condition that sidewalks be replaced in kind.

items.title: Flex Drive Services (Lyft Hub) Permits
items.summary: Referred a special permit for vehicle parking and a Class 2 dealer license to the Committee of the Whole to address concerns regarding the business model and potential traffic impacts.

items.title: Business Licenses and Food Truck Permit
items.summary: Approved a common victualler's license for Pinky’s Famous Pizza, a secondhand articles license for Roland's Jewelers, a Class 2 auto dealer license for Icon Motors Group, and a food truck permit for Neighborhood Produce.

items.title: Pro Repair Secondhand Articles License
items.summary: Referred the application to the Committee of the Whole for legal clarification on the scope of articles allowed under a secondhand license.

items.title: Senior Planner Position and Appropriation
items.summary: Approved the creation of a Senior Planner position for first reading but tabled the $55,267 appropriation for one week under Council Rule 21 due to concerns over fiscal accountability.

items.title: Finance Director Position and Step Increase
items.summary: Tabled the request to reclassify the Finance Director position and provide a step increase for one week under Council Rule 21.

items.title: Library Union Wage Amendment
items.summary: Approved a 2% annual base salary increase for all library union titles for fiscal years 2023 through 2025.

items.title: Park Renovation Grant Resolutions
items.summary: Approved resolutions authorizing the city to accept state grants for renovations at Carr Park and accessibility improvements at Gillis Park.

items.title: Parking Meter Installation and Costs
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the administration provide the costs of wrongly placed meter poles and remove installations on residential Boynton Road.

items.title: Work and Family Mobility Act Support
items.summary: Approved a resolution expressing support for Ballot Question 4 to allow residents to apply for state driver’s licenses regardless of immigration status.

items.title: Spending Moratorium and Fiscal Accountability
items.summary: Tabled a proposed spending moratorium for 30 days but approved a resolution requiring the Finance Director to attend a November meeting to provide quarterly reports and monthly warrant articles.

items.title: Administrative and Environmental Resolutions
items.summary: Approved resolutions regarding the MBTA bus network redesign, SeeClickFix referral procedures, the statewide mattress disposal ban, city job advertising, and Green Line bike path connections.

items.title: Code Enforcement and Tree Warden Definitions
items.summary: Referred the task of defining code enforcement officer and tree warden roles within the city ordinances to legal counsel.

items.title: Harvard Street Parking Changes
items.summary: Referred resident concerns regarding new 'No Parking' signage and a tow zone on Harvard Street to the Traffic Commission for review.

items.title: School Safety Communication
items.summary: Discussed the failure of the school administration to notify city councilors of a violent student assault at Medford High School and the resulting fear among students.
